draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Cabo de Rama Fort! Also called Praça do Cabo de Rama, it's a medieval hillfort in Khola village on the Canacona coast. It's one of the area's current favourites, quieter than the beaches and great for sweeping coastal views.
draft.hungryLine: There's not much to eat right at the fort, so head down to Palolem for Goan dishes and fish tandoor.

moodReplies.show-me-around: The fort is just a 3 minute walk, walk the walls and take in the coast.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Find a quiet corner of the fort and watch the sea, this is a spot for scenic views rather than crowds.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Beyond Palolem and Agonda, Canacona has nearly 20 lesser-known beaches, some reached only by a narrow track.

spots.name: Cabo de Rama Fort
spots.detail: 3 min walk · Medieval hillfort with big views of the coast

spots.name: Cotigao Wildlife Sanctuary
spots.detail: Short drive · A wildlife sanctuary in the Canacona area

tips.title: Bring your own transport.
tips.body: Public buses are few and far between out here, so come by bike or car.

tips.title: Come early for the views.
tips.body: The fort is all about scenic coastal views, so visit in the cooler hours and take your time.

story.title: Ancient Canacona
story.body: Down the coast in Loliem, a statue of Betal, possibly a pre-Hindu deity, may date to the seventh century or earlier. Canacona has four Betal deities in all.

story.title: A hillfort on the coast
story.body: Cabo de Rama Fort rose as a medieval hillfort in Khola village. Its Portuguese name is Praça do Cabo de Rama.

story.title: The coast is discovered
story.body: Canacona's beach belt was only 'discovered' after the 1990s. Today the fort, Palolem and Agonda are the area's hot favourites.
